title: AlphaGenome Decodes Non-Coding Regulatory DNA Across 1-Million-Base Windows
whyItMatters: Predicts how single-letter mutations anywhere in a 1-million-base-pair DNA window disrupt gene expression, splicing, and chromatin structure across the 98% non-coding human genome.
summary: Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome unified long-range sequence context (1 Mb) with single-base-pair output resolution, resolving a longstanding trade-off in computational genomics. Published in Nature in January 2026 and later expanded into the 9-billion-variant AlphaGenome Atlas, it enables geneticists to pinpoint disease-causing non-coding mutations that previously resisted experimental screening.
technicalHighlights: Simultaneously predicts thousands of molecular regulatory tracks—gene expression, RNA splicing, chromatin accessibility, and 3D contact maps—at single-base resolution.
Surpassed specialized state-of-the-art models across 22 of 24 variant-effect prediction benchmarks.
Peer-reviewed in Nature (Jan 2026) and expanded into a public predictive atlas covering 9 billion possible single-letter human DNA variants.
caveats: AlphaGenome 1 predicted bulk-tissue regulatory profiles rather than fine-grained individual cell states—a limitation subsequently addressed by AlphaGenome 2 in November 2026.

scoreRationale.foundational: Solved the sequence-length vs. single-base-resolution bottleneck for modeling non-coding human genome regulation.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly accelerates rare-disease diagnosis, cancer genomics, and non-coding therapeutic target discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Jan 2026) with broad public API and benchmark validation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Enabled an instant in-silico variant-impact atlas across all 9 billion human single-nucleotide substitutions.
